changelog.2.2.0: Optimized from v2.1.5: ~40% size reduction. Merged antiPatterns into qualityRules. Moved shared qualityGate checks to globalDefaults. Compressed mermaidCraft and refinementMode prose to directives. Removed redundant description fields. Zero functional changes.
changelog.2.2.1: BUGFIX: (1) User story deduplication — added refinementHint + idManagement to User Stories, expanded existingContent to cover structured items, added dedup qualityGate check. (2) linkStyle mismatch — flipped default to NO linkStyle, replaced coaching with procedural validation, added explicit excess-line deletion rule.

wordTargetInterpretation.target: IDEAL word count, NOT a minimum. Content that covers all points in fewer words is BETTER.
wordTargetInterpretation.max: Hard ceiling. Never exceed. Hitting max usually means bloat.
wordTargetInterpretation.zeroMeaning: target:0 + max:0 = table-only or diagram-only section, no prose limit.
wordTargetInterpretation.sweetSpot: 60-85% of target is the quality zone. If existing content covers all points below target, do NOT pad.

mermaidDefaults.hint: Short clean IDs (svc1, db1), human-readable names in labels. 3-5 words max per label.

mermaidCraft.philosophy: Simple diagram that renders > complex one that breaks. When in doubt, go simpler.
beforeDrawing: What ONE thing should this communicate? If you can't answer in one sentence, split the diagram.
Could a table work better? Linear sequences with no branching don't need diagrams.

renderingPitfalls.specialCharacters: Keep labels alphanumeric + spaces. Wrap in double quotes if special chars needed.
renderingPitfalls.labelLength: Max 5-6 words per node. Longer = explain in prose below, not in the node.
renderingPitfalls.edgeLabels: Max 2-3 words on arrows. Longer explanations go in prose.
renderingPitfalls.subgraphNesting: 1-2 levels reliable. 3+ levels = split into multiple diagrams.
renderingPitfalls.sequenceNotes: Keep very short. Long notes spanning participants often break.

linkStyleRule.default: DO NOT use linkStyle declarations. The default unstyled diagram is the correct output. An unstyled diagram that renders is always the right choice over a styled diagram that might break.
linkStyleRule.exception: ONLY add linkStyle if color-coding edges conveys essential meaning that cannot be expressed any other way (e.g., red for error paths vs green for happy paths in a flow that shows both). Decorative styling is never a valid reason.
linkStyleRule.procedure: IF linkStyle is used, follow this exact procedure: (1) Write ALL node definitions and ALL connections first. (2) Count the total number of connections (each -->, --->, -.->  etc. is one link). Call this N. (3) Valid linkStyle indices are 0 through N-1 ONLY. (4) Write linkStyle declarations referencing ONLY indices 0 through N-1. (5) If the count doesn't match after writing — DELETE the excess linkStyle lines from the end. Do NOT try to renumber or recount — just remove the extras. Fewer styled links is always safe; extra indices always break.
linkStyleRule.onRefinement: If editing an existing diagram's connections (adding or removing any -->  or similar): DELETE ALL existing linkStyle declarations entirely rather than trying to reindex. If styling is still needed, recount from scratch following the procedure above.

checks: NO linkStyle declarations present (default). If present, confirm they follow linkStyleRule.procedure.
Every node ID in connections exists as a defined node (svc1 vs srv1 typos create phantom nodes)
Every class applied to a node has a matching classDef — if unsure, remove the class application

mermaidCraft.recovery: Diagram failing? Strip to 3-4 core nodes, get it rendering, add back one element at a time.

globalDefaults.raciRules: Each row: exactly ONE Accountable. Bold the R and A cells.

riskLevels.full: Heat map (5×5 colored emoji) + register table + contingency column
riskLevels.standard: Register table: Risk, Likelihood, Impact, Mitigation, Owner
riskLevels.light: Simple risk table, no heat map or scoring

refinementMode.corePrinciple: Refinement = TIGHTEN, not EXPAND. More signal per sentence, fewer total sentences.

targets: Throat-clearing: 'It is important to note...', 'As mentioned above...'
Hedging: 'We believe that...', 'It is worth considering...'
Generic truths: 'Testing is important', 'Security must be considered'

examples: TLS 1.3 transit, AES-256 at rest, least-privilege IAM
Checkout <90s, zero full-page reloads, WCAG 2.1 AA

restructure.rule: Move misplaced content to correct section. Never duplicate — move.

refinementMode.lengthRule: Output must be SAME length or SHORTER than input. >10% longer = refinement failed.
refinementMode.singletonFields: Generated on / Last Updated / Status / Owner: scan existing doc, UPDATE in place, never append duplicates.
refinementMode.existingContent: Before generating any diagram, table, or NUMBERED/ID'd ITEMS (user stories, requirements, risks), scan for existing ones in same section. If they exist: update in place. Never produce duplicates alongside originals. For ID'd items (US-{nn}, FR-{nnn}, RISK-{nnn}, BR-{nnn}): scan all existing IDs, preserve them, continue sequential numbering only if genuinely new items needed.

sentence: Every sentence must pass the 'so what?' test — removable without loss = shouldn't exist
No throat-clearing openers: 'It is important to...', 'It should be noted...', 'We need to ensure...'
Active voice: 'Service processes 10K req/min' not 'Requests are processed by the service'
Lead with the specific, follow with context
section: No section repeats info from another section
Tables don't need prose preambles restating what the table shows
Section with only generic advice = empty. Fill with project-specific content or remove.
document: Objective alone should let reader decide whether to keep reading
2-minute scan (per progressiveDisclosure) must cover scope, key decisions, risks
Consistent terminology throughout — same name for same thing everywhere
antiPatterns: Echo Padding: restating Objective in other sections with different words → delete, start with section's own first point
Filler Bullets: 'Ensure high availability', 'Follow best practices' → replace with measurable specifics or delete
Hedge Stacking: multiple qualifiers per sentence → make direct statement or move to Open Questions
Premature Elaboration: 'Kubernetes, a container orchestration platform...' → use term directly, Glossary if needed
Table Narration: prose describing what a table already shows → delete, one-line insight only if non-obvious
Section Filler: 'This section describes...' / 'In summary...' → delete, start and end with substance
Symmetric Padding: adding weak items to match other lists' length → 3 strong bullets > 6 half-filler

qualityGateShared.hint: These checks apply to ALL templates, both generation and refinement.
checks: Mermaid diagrams: NO linkStyle declarations by default. If present, verify indices 0 to N-1 match actual link count exactly — if mismatch, DELETE excess linkStyle lines from end
All node IDs in diagram connections are defined, all subgraphs closed, all applied classes have classDefs
refinement: 'Generated on' / 'Last Updated' appears exactly ONCE in Epic Status table — updated in place, not duplicated
Existing mermaid diagrams updated in place — no duplicate diagrams unless template requires multiple
If diagram connections were added/removed, DELETE ALL linkStyle declarations rather than reindexing
ID'd items (US-{nn}, FR-{nnn}, RISK-{nnn}, BR-{nnn}): existing IDs preserved, no duplicates generated, new IDs continue sequentially from max existing
Output same length or shorter than input
All specific numbers, dates, names preserved
Vague statements replaced with specific ones, not just reworded

Requirements.hint: 30–80 words per requirement. Priority emoji for scanning. IDs: BR-{nnn}.

Objective.hint: What user problem are we solving, and how will we know we've solved it?
Objective.example: Enable users to save and reuse delivery addresses, reducing checkout abandonment by 15% and average checkout time from 4.2 minutes to under 90 seconds for returning customers.

Problem Statement.hint: Lead with evidence — user research data, support tickets, funnel drop-off rates. Not assumptions.

User Stories.template:
**US-{nn}: {title}**
As a [persona], I want [action] so that [outcome]
**Acceptance Criteria:** [testable criterion]

count.refinementBehavior: If stories already exist, count.min is already satisfied. Do NOT generate new stories to meet min. Only add a story if there is a genuine gap in user coverage not addressed by any existing story.

idManagement.format: US-{nn} where nn is zero-padded two-digit sequential (US-01, US-02, US-03)
idManagement.onGenerate: Start at US-01, increment sequentially. No gaps.
idManagement.onRefine: Scan ALL existing US-{nn} IDs first. Preserve existing IDs exactly. If a new story is genuinely needed, continue from max existing ID + 1 (e.g., existing US-01 to US-05 → next is US-06). NEVER use offset numbering (US-100, US-1001). NEVER regenerate stories that overlap in scope with existing ones.
idManagement.deduplication: Two stories are duplicates if they describe the same user performing the same action for the same outcome, even if worded differently. During refinement: if duplicate found, keep the one with better acceptance criteria and remove the other. Do not keep both.

User Stories.hint: Each story MUST begin with bold title 'US-01: One-Click Reorder'. Unique, concise, action-oriented. Maps to testable acceptance criteria.
User Stories.example:
**US-01: Save Delivery Address**
As a returning customer, I want to save my delivery address so that I don't have to re-enter it on every order.
**Acceptance Criteria:** Save up to 5 addresses; selectable at checkout; editable/deletable in account settings.
User Stories.refinementHint: CRITICAL: Scan existing user stories BEFORE making any changes. Preserve all existing story IDs and content. Do NOT generate new stories that duplicate the scope of existing ones. If existing stories cover the requirements adequately, improve their wording and acceptance criteria in place — do not add new stories. The only valid reason to add a story during refinement is a genuine coverage gap where no existing story addresses a required user need.

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: Be explicit about what's out for V1 and deferred to V2.

Functional Requirements.hint: Atomic (one testable behavior per row), reference User Story by ID (US-01). IDs: FR-{nnn}.

User Flows.hint: Happy path AND key error paths. Don't just document the sunshine scenario.

Launch Plan.hint: Feature flag strategy, rollout %, rollback criteria, A/B test design if applicable.

UX/Design.hint: Link to Figma/mockups. Key interaction patterns and a11y requirements.

feature_specification.description: Feature specs bridging product and engineering — evidence-based problems, user stories with acceptance criteria, edge cases, launch plans, measurable success.
qualityGate: Problem Statement leads with evidence (data, tickets, metrics) — not assumptions
Every User Story has bold US-{nn} title, sequential numbering (US-01, US-02...), no gaps, no offset numbering (US-100, US-1001)
Every User Story maps to at least one Functional Requirement via ID — no orphan stories
Edge Cases: at least 5 scenarios — fewer = happy-path bias
NFRs use specific numbers, not adjectives
Launch Plan includes rollback criteria
No generic filler like 'ensure a good user experience'
No duplicate user stories: no two stories describe the same user performing the same action. If US-01 and US-06 cover the same scope, one must be removed.
